newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed, helped by stocks.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed, helped by stocks.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday, though the sharp fall in U.S. stocks and bonds provided some support and increased the chances for a rally going into the year-end, traders said.
"Precious metals opened higher and found some support from the weaker stock market, but then saw some serious dealer selling," FIMAT New York trader John Tyree said.
"Volumes were a bit better and some traders are hoping for a shortcovering rally as the year winds down, as funds take profits on the year's downtrend, but overall the tone is still anemic," he said.
COMEX February gold ended up 10 cents at $370.60, well off its session high at $372.00. Estimated total volume in gold was 28,000 lots.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.60/369.10, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $368.25, and the New York close Tuesday at $368.40/80.
COMEX March silver futures closed down 1.2 cents at $4.860 an ounce, after seeing early highs at $4.790.
Concern about Japanese disinvestment and a change of policy on the yen, was behind the volatility in world stock and bond markets, traders said.
"If the Dow fails to fight back near the close and ends sharply lower, I think gold will come in tomorrow with a better tone again," said Anthony Raia, a trader with Linnco Futures Group in Chicago.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 97 points at 6,376 a half hour before the stock market close.
"Then we've got January gold and silver options expiring Friday and we may see some fund shortcovering before the year-end also," he said.

"I think a small rally is possible from here, but any move in gold always seems to come to an end around ... Valentine's Day (February 14), and the current year-long downtrend now projects down to around $356 in gold where it would start to look cheap," he said.
Spot gold peaked at five-year highs at $417.70 an ounce on February 2 this year, before beginning its year long decline to three-year lows at $366 on December 3.

Longer term though precious metals markets needed a sharp correction in U.S. equity markets of at least five to 10 percent to encourage investment demand back into gold as a portfolio diversifier, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum ended up 70 cents at $372.40 an ounce, while NYMEX March palladium closed up $1.20 at $122.25.
The April platinum/April gold spread recovered to $1.70 an ounce, from a six week low at 50 cents an ounce Monday, after seeing a high $9.40 on November 21.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk,+1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
